This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study (I5) of schizophrenia patients and matched controls (I8). It reports within-task emotion contrast (negative vs neutral olfactory stimulation) (I9) and provides group-level whole-brain results with peak coordinates/tables (I10, I11). However, it does NOT meet critical eligibility requirements for this review: the emotional stimuli are olfactory (odorants), not VISUAL, so I7 is not met. Also, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no emotion-regulation instruction such as reappraisal/acceptance/distancing), so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply to this report. Because inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to perform cognitive reappraisal (interpretation/reinterpretation via contextual titles) of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (young adult university participants) is eligible. The fMRI analysis includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (IAPS2–IAPS1 for up-/down-regulation) and reports group-level whole-brain activation results with peak coordinates (e.g., left middle temporal gyrus coordinates provided; Table 2 referenced). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not review-only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without within-task effects, not an empathy task lacking regulation instructions). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: reappraisal and acceptance), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I11 (results reported with coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (visual stimuli requirement). Exclusion criteria applied: none (E3–E7 not triggered). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (Increase, Decrease, Look) during visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures and high-arousal film clips). It reports within-task contrasts (Increase>Look, Decrease>Look, Increase>Decrease), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE correction, and includes methods, results, and discussion. All review inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (distancing reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The sample includes a participant group (male marijuana users) with matched controls and reports group-level results (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., "distance > baseline", "spontaneous_negative > baseline") (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE and peak coordinates are reported in standard (MNI) space (I10), and results are clearly described in text, figures, and coordinate lists (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not non-empirical (E3), not ROI-only (E4), not connectivity-only without task activation (E5), not only between-group contrasts without within-group effects (E6), and not an empathy/perspective paradigm without emotion-regulation instruction (E7).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation strategy) using visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Look-Negative) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE correction. The sample (clinical patients with GAD, SAD, MDD) is acceptable per inclusion criteria, and the full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-task contrasts are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal to downregulate emotions (meets I5 and I6). Emotional stimuli were visual pictures (neutral, fear, OCD-related) (I7). Participant groups include OCD patients and unrelated healthy controls with separate reporting, and unaffected siblings (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (fear regulate > attend; OCD regulate > attend; fear > neutral; OCD > neutral) and within-group regulation effects (I9). The manuscript references and presents whole-brain analyses and supplemental whole-brain results with MNI coordinates (tables and supplement), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no review-only, ROI-only, or connectivity-only reporting; within-group effects are reported; not an empathy/perspective-only task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal via distancing to downregulate emotion (meets I5,I6). Stimuli were visual pictures (negative, positive, neutral), meeting I7. Sample includes acute AN patients and matched healthy controls with group results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and viewing (negative watch > neutral; negative watch > negative distance; negative watch < negative distance) (I9). Group-level voxelwise analyses and whole-brain/exploratory results with peak coordinates are reported (figures/Supplementary, coordinate peaks in text), satisfying I10 and I11. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion; no exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects, not an empathy task). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) during presentation of visual stimuli (complex social images/IAPS). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., reappraise > look-negative, look-negative > reappraise) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look-negative > look-neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with voxelwise FDR correction and MNI coordinates/tables. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (static angry face photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Observe-angry, Increase > Observe-angry), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample is healthy adults and resting-state subset is reported but task analyses meet meta-analysis objectives. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs participants to generate cognitive reappraisals (downregulate anger) — i.e., an emotion regulation strategy — satisfying the review focus on reappraisal. Emotional stimuli included photographs (presented with audio stories), qualifying as visual stimuli. The paper reports within-task contrasts (RGT > fixation; RGT > AUT) and whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with voxelwise FWE correction and reported activation coordinates/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and the study should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed cognitive reappraisal (I6) using visual IAPS images (I7) in a healthy adult sample (I8) and reports a within-task contrast (ReappNeg vs LookNeg) (I9). However, the full text presents analyses based on ROI-extracted beta weights (AAL ROIs) submitted to PCA and discriminant analysis, and does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with peak coordinates in standard space (no tables/figures of whole-brain peaks or coordinates are provided). Therefore it appears to report ONLY ROI-based results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis, which meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map with coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: E4. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative) and an unregulated viewing contrast (Attend Negative > Attend Neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and FWE cluster correction. Sample (n=62 young adults) is eligible. Although resting-state analyses are also included, the paper clearly contains task activation results, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs participants in two regulation-related conditions (attention shifting: indoor/outdoor; appraisal/labeling: like/dislike) in addition to an implicit viewing condition. Stimuli are visual static composite images (faces/scenes). Participants are healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (male/female–face-only; indoor/outdoor–male/female; like/dislike–male/female) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (MNI) and FWE correction. Full article includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (cues and proportion displays) (I7). Sample is adult non-clinical participants (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing anticipation of difficult vs. easy visual cues (an unregulated viewing contrast) and reports whole-brain group analyses with coordinates (I9, I10, I11). However, the study did not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance or other instructed regulation) at any point, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task contrasts (Regulate vs Attend). However, the paper reports ROI-based task activation analyses (extracted mean BOLD in predefined spherical ROIs) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain task activation reporting) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain task analysis). Summary: exclusion criteria met: E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal/distancing as an emotion regulation strategy during presentation of visual stimuli (I6,I7). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Look-Negative; Look-Negative > Look-Neutral) used for analyses (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and family-wise-error correction (P < .05 FWE) (I10), and these whole-brain results and coordinates are described in the text/tables (I11). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within-group effects reported; not an empathy-only perspective task).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (increase/decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (static face photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation to view ([increase + decrease] > view) and describes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and identified peak regions (reported in tables). The sample includes both patients with lifetime MDD and matched healthy controls with results reported across/within groups. These features satisfy all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5–I11). The full text provided contains methods, results, and tables/figures described, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotions evoked by visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (regulate > view), performs group-level whole-brain GLM analyses with results transformed to Talairach space and provides activation coordinates (Tables/Figures). Sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to voluntarily generate (up-regulate) a positive mood while viewing visual stimuli (happy facial expressions) and using autobiographical memory. It reports within-task analyses using activation during the happy mood induction blocks (regression of PANAS change with brain activation), group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with MNI peak coordinates and cluster tables, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. All inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met (task-based fMRI, instructed regulation/up-regulation during visual stimuli, visual stimuli used, eligible sample, within-task activation/contrast analyses, and whole-brain coordinate reporting). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) during stimulus viewing (I6), uses visual stimuli (IAPS and photographs) (I7), includes a developmental sample (ages 6–23) which is an eligible sample (I8), reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraisal/Negative > Reactivity/Negative) (I9), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholds (I10,I11). The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears to be a complete full text. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore I recommend inclusion.

This full text meets the review’s criteria for inclusion as an unregulated viewing fMRI study. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (I7: IAPS/static grayscale images) and includes an unregulated viewing contrast (Negative > Neutral) reported in voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analyses (I9, I10). Results are presented in tables and figures with voxelwise thresholds and reported regions (I11). Sample includes a clinical group and controls (I8). The task was an emotional oddball requiring attention to targets amid emotional distractors; no instruction to regulate emotion was given, so the study does not meet I6 (instructed emotion regulation), but I6 is not required because the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts per I9. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, or empathy/perspective-taking tasks) apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion as an unregulated visual-emotion task with whole-brain activation contrasts.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (‘Think Objectively’ vs ‘Watch’) using visual IAPS images in a within-subject randomized design. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise negative > watch negative) and second-level group analyses with peak activations and cluster statistics (tables/figures; seed coordinate [−20 −4 −20] and cluster extents reported), and reports voxelwise functional connectivity (gPPI) results linked to behavior. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply (no non-empirical paper, not ROI-only, reports within-task contrasts, not resting-state-only, and includes explicit regulation instructions). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (self-focused increase and decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (anger facial photographs). The paper reports behavioral and neural within-task contrasts (e.g., increase > view-angry, decrease > view-angry, view-angry > view-neutral), provides whole-brain group-level results with anatomical localization and tables/figures in standard space, and reports patient and healthy control groups separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is appropriate for meta-analysis.

This full-text reports a task-based BOLD fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal ("Reduce Emotion") vs maintain responses to negative images (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (I7). Participant groups include healthy controls and clinical groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Baseline; Maintain vs Baseline; and task effects/interaction) and behavioral-fMRI relationships (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented with cluster thresholds and peak coordinates in Talairach space (I10), and results are reported in tables/figures/supplement (I11). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; reports whole-brain task activation maps; not only connectivity or ROI-only; includes within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This full-text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression (I6). Emotional stimuli were visual static images from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes a clinical group (schizophrenia) and healthy controls, with task results reported for patient group (I8). The analyses report within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > attend negative; suppress > attend negative) (I9). Whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed and reported (cluster-level FWE correction), with results presented in text/figures/tables consistent with standard MNI coordinates (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity-only results). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore include in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs explicit emotion regulation strategies (Compassion meditation and Reappraisal) during an emotion-regulation task (preparation and implementation periods). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative, Reappraisal > Watch-Negative) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction, with results presented in tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; reports within-group effects; not purely perspective-taking without regulation).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (Increase and Decrease) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (film clips), satisfying the intervention/strategy requirement. This is a task-based fMRI study (N=30) that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). Although this is a task-based fMRI study with an instructed reappraisal/perspective-taking regulation strategy (meets I5, I6), includes an appropriate sample (I8), reports within-task regulation-related contrasts (I9) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses/coordinates (I10, I11), it does NOT meet the required stimulus modality criterion: the emotional content consists of monetary decision outcomes and numeric gamble displays rather than visual emotional stimuli (e.g., IAPS images, faces, or film/video). The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs participants to use cognitive regulation (consider long-term consequences vs. immediate consumption) while viewing visual food images. It reports within-task regulation contrasts (LATER > NOW and related contrasts), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics, and includes full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adult women) is eligible. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis eligibility for emotion regulation fMRI with visual stimuli and instructed cognitive control.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes an attentional-control implicit regulation task. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Look-Negative; Threat Low > Threat High) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE correction. This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use two emotion-regulation strategies (Observe — a mindfulness/acceptance instruction — and Suppress) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Suppress-negative vs. Look-negative; Observe-negative vs. Look-negative; Look-negative vs. Look-neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholding described. This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive self-distancing/reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The methods describe standard SPM8 whole-brain preprocessing and GLM contrasts (e.g., US-Paired: CER>NoCER) used to define PFC seeds and report ROI coordinates (ventral striatum center x=26,y=6,z=-8), and the Results present within-task regulation contrasts and connectivity effects. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply (no non-empirical article, not limited to only ROI/connectivity without whole-brain task maps, and within-task contrasts are reported). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli in an adolescent sample and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts (appetitive > aversive) with peak coordinates. However, participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); rather, they performed an inhibitory go/no-go task while emotional images were presented as incidental distractors. Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy). All other relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11), and no exclusion criteria from the list apply. Because I6 is not met, the study must be excluded.

Full-text reports a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Look conditions) with visual IAPS images, single-trial/block contrasts (Look-Negative>Look-Neutral; Reappraise>Look-Neutral), and a whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis reporting MNI peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results. The sample includes a clinical GAD group and healthy controls with results reported separately. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore complete. Meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This full text describes an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the record is complete.

The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and acceptance) during presentation of visual sad images (IAPS and normed photos). The paper reports within-task contrasts (accept > reappraise, accept > view, reappraise > view) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported cluster results/locations in tables and text. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Although an a priori mask/SVC was noted for some analyses, whole-brain clusters outside frontal/amygdala (e.g., insula) are reported, supporting whole-brain task-evoked results. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (disorder-related > neutral) and an exploratory whole-brain analysis with reported activation clusters/tables, and includes both a clinical (SAD) group and healthy controls. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis criteria for unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using a visual emotional task (approach–avoidance with happy/angry face images) in human participants (police recruits). The task includes explicit instructions requiring cognitive control over automatic emotional action tendencies (incongruent vs. congruent blocks), and the primary neural contrasts reported (incongruent > congruent) index instructed emotional control. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and also reports psychophysiological-interaction connectivity analyses. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI of instructed emotion regulation/control with visual stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain results.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s stimulus and whole-brain reporting requirements. It is a task-based fMRI study with instructed self-regulation (rtfMRI neurofeedback using autobiographical recall) and reports within-task contrasts and ROI/effective-connectivity results; however, the regulated stimuli are internally generated autobiographical memories rather than externally presented visual emotional stimuli (violating I7). The paper focuses on ROI-based and effective-connectivity (VAR/SVAR) analyses and does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map with peak coordinates (violating I10) and thus falls under exclusions for reporting only ROI/seed-based connectivity/effective-connectivity results (E5) and ROI-only/partial-coverage results (E4). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results (including amygdala and vlPFC) and includes tables/figures/supplemental material describing whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (sad and neutral film clips) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Sad > Neutral). Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported with peak coordinates in standard space, and the full article includes methods, results, and discussion. The study therefore meets the review’s scope (studies of viewing visual emotional stimuli without regulation) and satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study uses visual (face) stimuli and reports the unregulated contrast (match faces vs. match shapes) and whole-brain subject-specific contrast maps, and includes healthy adult participants and behavioral measures of perceived stress and inattention. However, the fMRI task did NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy (implicit reappraisal was inferred rather than instructed), so it fails inclusion criterion I6. Additionally, the paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (no whole-brain peak coordinates/tables are provided in the main text), so it fails I10. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed regulation), I10 (no group-level whole-brain map with coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (explicit suppression) and uses priming for implicit suppression during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and other images). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing suppression runs to baseline (e.g., EXP vs BASEEXP), Dm (subsequent memory) contrasts, group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with tables/clusters and ROI analyses, and peak coordinates. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual stimuli (IAPS) with within-task contrasts (EXP neg > neut, PRES neg > neut) and reports peak coordinates (meeting I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11), it does NOT instruct participants to implement an emotion-regulation strategy during scanning. The study selects participants on habitual use of reappraisal vs. suppression (ERQ) and examines correlations with activation, but there is no instructed regulation condition (failure to meet I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore it must be excluded because it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I6 (fMRI task with instructed emotion regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual facial stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts, but it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy during scanning (I6 not met). The paper uses an ROI-focused analysis (family-wise error within predefined ROIs) and presents ROI-derived coordinates rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map, so it lacks qualifying whole-brain results (I10 not met) and thus meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study cannot be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly matches the review objective. It instructs cognitive emotion regulation (socially-induced reappraisal/distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures), reports within-task contrasts (Social-Reg > Social-Look; Self-Reg > Self-Look), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that includes an instructed emotion-regulation condition: affect labeling (participants verbally label facial emotions), which functions as an incidental/instructed regulation strategy (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual (static face images) (I7). The sample includes patient (methamphetamine-dependent) and control groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (affect label vs affect match; and emotion viewing contrasts) (I9). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and tables of clusters/coordinates are provided (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity), includes within-group effects, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study must be excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met): participants performed a color-naming/ignore-the-word task rather than being instructed to reappraise, accept, distance, or otherwise regulate their emotional response. Stimuli are word stimuli (visual words), which are explicitly excluded by the review criterion (I7 not met: the review requires visual images/films; word/sentence stimuli are excluded). The study also does not report a within-task contrast of instructed emotion regulation vs viewing (I9 not met): reported contrasts are unpleasant vs neutral (emotional interference) and connectivity analyses, not regulate>view or similar. It does satisfy I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps with standard-space coordinates) and I11 (coordinates/tables reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation in older adults that reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. However, the regulated stimuli are personalized worry/suppression sentences (script-driven imagery / word/sentence prompts presented on the screen) rather than visual emotional stimuli (e.g., pictures, faces, film). Inclusion criterion I7 requires visual emotional stimuli and specifically excludes studies using word or sentence stimuli or purely script-driven imagery. Therefore the study fails to meet I7 and must be excluded. Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: worry suppression), I8 (eligible sample: elderly clinical + controls), I9 (reports within-task contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to maintain versus not maintain their emotional state (an instructed emotion-control/manipulation strategy), using visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts comparing maintain > non-maintain (and emotion > neutral), conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports peak coordinates, and includes an adult sample with results at the group level. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This article meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal: “decrease negative”) during presentation of stimuli (I6). Stimuli were visual static images (negative and neutral pictures) (I7). The sample includes clinical (female adolescents with conduct disorder) and typically developing control groups reported separately (I8). Analyses report within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (decrease negative > look negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look negative > look neutral) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted and whole-brain familywise-error-corrected results are reported (cluster-level FWE and references to peak/cluster reports), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, within-group effects are reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) presented as distractors during a delayed working-memory task. The paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative emotional > scrambled) and within-group as well as between-group whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (FWE-corrected), and provides full methods, results and discussion. The sample includes OCD patients and matched healthy controls with within-group effects reported. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraisal) was given, the meta-analysis objective allows inclusion of studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; the study therefore provides an appropriate unregulated emotion contrast for inclusion. Connectivity analyses (DCM) are present but whole-brain task activations are also reported, so exclusion criterion E5 does not apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use causal attributions as an emotion-regulation strategy while viewing visual stimuli (static facial images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (internal>view, external>view, emotion-specific contrasts) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and reported coordinates/tables. Participant groups (MDD and matched healthy controls) are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging, preprocessing, statistics), Results (behavioral, fMRI, connectivity) and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, includes task activation maps, includes within-group effects, and the instructed task explicitly directs emotion regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). All relevant inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed emotion regulation (look, increase, decrease) using cognitive reappraisal strategies (I6). Stimuli were visual (IAPS and in-house disgusting images) (I7). The sample includes children/adolescents with ASD and TD controls (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-gross vs. look-gross; increase-gross vs. look-gross) (I9). It performed group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and references coordinate tables/figures (Table S2, figures) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical with original fMRI task activation maps (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because inclusion criterion I7 is NOT met: the emotional stimuli regulated are text/sentences (participant-generated autobiographical scripts and flashed negative self-belief statements), which the review’s criteria define as non-visual and thus excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—cognitive reappraisal), I8 (sample includes clinical group with separate control group reporting), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g., reappraise > react), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with standard-space coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete = false).

The full text meets all inclusion requirements for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; Suppress condition) during stimulus presentation (I6). Stimuli are visual (IAPS static images; I7). The sample is healthy adult participants (I8). The analyses report within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Suppress > Maintain, Maintain > Suppress) and parametric covariates of subjective ratings (I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with peak coordinates in standard space are reported (I10,I11). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation issues). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only resting-state/effective connectivity analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: participant groups reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task; no cognitive reappraisal or other regulation instruction), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli—resting-state with eyes closed), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps reported). The article is a complete full-text report of a resting-state sDCM connectivity study and thus does not address the meta-analysis objective of task-based emotion regulation with visual stimuli. Full text appears complete for screening purposes (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, maintain) during recall of previously encoded visual images (IAPS). Methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with coordinates/tables and contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., decrease>maintain, increase>maintain, conjunctions, phase-specific contrasts). Sample is healthy young adults and within-task contrasts are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study that uses instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: downregulate and upregulate) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (healthy participants; genotype groups reported) is acceptable, and the paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (downregulate > look, upregulate > look, negative > neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster thresholds in standard space, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met.

The article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) during presentation of visual negative and neutral pictures, satisfying I5–I7. The sample is healthy adult participants (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (RegulateNeg > WatchNeg and WatchNeg > RegulateNeg) and associated behavioral ratings (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (I10), and results are reported in text/figures/tables (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain activation results (not ROI-only), is not a non-empirical paper, and does not report only connectivity or only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI emotion regulation with visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs a cognitive regulation strategy (thought suppression/self-distraction) and reports whole-brain group analyses with coordinates; however it does NOT meet the meta-analysis requirement that the regulated emotional stimuli be visual. The paradigm uses anticipatory anxiety for painful electrical stimulation with auditory cues and somatosensory (pain) stimuli, so I7 (visual stimuli) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (96 IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Look) and provides peak coordinates (MNI) for activation and connectivity results, satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, imaging acquisition/analysis), Results (behavioral and fMRI), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal via distancing) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS and matched photographs). The sample (ages 10.5–22.9) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (regulation/negative > reactivity/negative) and unregulated viewing (reactivity/negative > reactivity/neutral), and conducts whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space. Reporting of coordinates and methods is detailed in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, includes task activation maps, not connectivity-only, not an empathy task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal (Regulate) strategy versus a control (Attend) during a sequential investment task. The stimuli are visual market displays presented on-screen and evoke emotional/regret responses related to financial decisions. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Regulate and Attend and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates (MNI) and thresholding, plus tables in Supporting Information. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an instructed emotion-regulation (reappraisal) task using visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing high-control (reappraise) vs low-control (rate) and presents whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with peak coordinates (tables and figures). Sample qualifies (healthy adults). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal to increase and decrease negative affect) using visual stimuli (IAPS photographs). The sample (healthy female participants) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (increase > look, decrease > look, look > decrease) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Full text is complete and includes methods, results, and discussion. Accordingly, it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal by distancing) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS interpersonal images). Behavioral and imaging results report within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. distance > look; look > distance; negative > neutral) and interaction contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster tables in standard (MNI) space; small-volume correction was used only for the amygdala in addition to whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs voluntary emotion regulation (detachment/distancing) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample comprises healthy adult participants and within-task contrasts (regulated vs. non-regulated; negative vs. neutral) are reported. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (with peak coordinates and FWE correction), and amygdala ROI results are also provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (Detachment, Reinterpretation, Distraction, Expressive Suppression) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., ‘Regulate Negative’ > ‘Permit Negative’ and vice versa), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and presents full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adults) is eligible. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly used a cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) paradigm with instructed regulation (Suppress/reappraise) and a passive Observe condition. Emotional stimuli were visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (Maintain>Observe and Suppress>Maintain) and describes group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with correction and supplementary tables for full results/coordinates. The sample includes cocaine-dependent groups and a healthy control group with group results reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced but their absence does not render the main text incomplete.

This study is excluded because the emotional stimulus is auditory script-driven imagery rather than a visual stimulus, and participants were instructed to imagine the script (vividness) rather than to perform an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample including patient and control groups), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts such as ‘trigger vs baseline’), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (stimuli are non-visual — audio script-driven imagery). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Maintain vs Reappraisal) using visual IAPS images, reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Reappraise), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. The sample (patients with panic disorder, randomized to treatment vs waiting) is acceptable per inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (study does not report only ROI/SVC or only connectivity; whole-brain analyses are present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (Reduce vs Maintain) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reduce > Maintain and related effects), presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-correction (AlphaSim) and tables/figures of significant clusters, and includes an eligible sample (anxious and control groups). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within-task effects are reported; not an empathy/perspective task without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, view) while viewing visual threat-related images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (increase>view, decrease>view), trial-by-trial correlations, and group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present. Sample (healthy adult females) is eligible. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not connectivity-only, not ROI-only reporting).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use distraction (MEMORIZE condition) versus passive viewing to regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS and EmoPics), with female BPD patients and control groups reported separately. The analysis includes within-task contrasts (NEGATIVE>NEUTRAL; MEMORIZE vs VIEW) and group×time×task contrasts, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) while presenting visual IAPS pictures to healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion induction and regulation (e.g., view NEG – view NEU; view NEG – distract; view NEG – reappraise) and provides peak coordinates in MNI space. The manuscript also states that complementary exploratory whole-brain analyses (Supplementary Table 1) are provided, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (coordinates reported in text/tables/supplement). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, non-empirical, connectivity-only analyses) apply.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual face stimuli in an appropriate sample (I5, I7, I8, I10 satisfied), it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (I6 not met). The task involves impression formation and social-cognitive evaluation rather than an emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraise, accept, distance). While condition>baseline contrasts were modeled for use in PLS, the study does not report within-task contrasts of emotion regulation nor an explicit unregulated viewing contrast of emotional stimuli (I9 not met). The study therefore falls outside the review scope; it also meets exclusion criterion E7 (social/perspective-taking/impression-formation without instruction to amplify or dampen one’s emotional response). Excluded because E7 applies; inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10; inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (movie clips and proposal screens) in an Ultimatum Game. The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., unfair > fair) and decision contrasts, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported peak activations (tables/figures). The sample (healthy young adult women) is acceptable. Although the study does not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal), the review objective includes studies that involve unregulated viewing; thus the study meets the review’s criteria for inclusion.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal (MAINTAIN/INCREASE/DECREASE) with visual IAPS images, includes both a patient (BPD) and healthy control group with separate reporting, presents within-task contrasts (DECREASE>MAINTAIN, INCREASE>MAINTAIN, negative>neutral), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/tables. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

Full text shows a task-based fMRI study that instructed emotion-regulation strategies (feel, accept, analyze) and reports whole-brain group analyses and within-task regulation contrasts. However, the emotional stimuli are autobiographical memories cued by words/phrases (script-driven imagery), not visual stimuli (no pictures, faces, scenes, or film). Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based emotion regulation fMRI. It reports resting-state fMRI (seed-based rs-FC and spDCM) and behavioral ratings from an Emotion Processing Task performed outside the scanner; there is no task-based fMRI acquisition or within-task emotion-regulation instructions/contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (reports only resting-state/seed/effective connectivity without task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS pictures) and I8 (sample: elderly adults acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy during fMRI/task), I9 (reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts), I10 (whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation coordinates). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which children (8–12 yrs) were instructed to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (“MAKE-POSITIVE”) while viewing visual sad images (IAPS and child-appropriate photos). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise sad vs. view sad; view sad vs. view neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with corrected thresholds) as well as ROI analyses. Core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate appetitive responses to visually presented food images (static photographs). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Regulate Craved > Look Craved, Regulate > Look) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Look Craved > Look Not Craved, Look Craved > Look Neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-correction parameters and peak coordinates; small-ROI results for the ventral striatum are also noted but whole-brain results are primary. The sample includes adolescents (10–23 years) and results are presented in sufficient methodological and results detail (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal with visual IAPS images in healthy adults, and it reports within-task condition comparisons. However, the fMRI analysis summarizes activation in AAL ROIs rather than reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or peak coordinates in standard space. The paper explicitly notes use of AAL ROIs and that voxel-level/whole-brain maps are not provided. Therefore it violates exclusion E4 (only ROI-based results / no whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (whole-brain evidence) and thus I11 is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images and facial displays) in an appropriate adult sample and reports within-task contrasts (Look vs Decrease; Match vs Label). However, all activation effects are reported using ROI-based analyses (amygdala ROIs) and PPI connectivity analyses restricted to anatomically defined IFG masks. The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (analyses were mask-restricted), so it fails inclusion criterion I10 and (by implication) I11. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI / small-volume-corrected results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise > look contrasts) and reports within-task contrasts. Stimuli include visual faces (fearful and neutral) used during the instruction/regulation period; although top-down generation used sentences as background, the regulated stimulus during instruction is a visual face, so the study meets the visual-stimuli requirement. The sample (healthy adult women) is acceptable. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to employ an emotion regulation strategy. Instead, subjects performed a spatial cueing task and were told that faces were irrelevant (i.e., passive/ignored viewing), so no instructed regulation (reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, etc.) occurred. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — faces), I8 (sample acceptable — older and young adults), I9 (reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing; emotion vs neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported), I11 (results described adequately). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 violations). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded solely due to failure to meet I6 (instructed emotion regulation).

This article meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs explicit emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and distraction (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes remitted MDD patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported (I8). Analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraisal vs. view; distraction vs. view) and viewing contrasts (I9). The paper reports group-level activation peaks in standard (MNI) space (e.g., amygdala coordinates) and thresholding information, consistent with whole-brain/voxelwise reporting (I10,I11). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

The study is a task-based fMRI/ASL investigation of worry induction and instructed reappraisal in older adults and reports whole-brain voxelwise results. This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (food images) in an adolescent sample, and it reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > imagine eating) and whole-brain analyses. This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (self-focused distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) in healthy adult participants. This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study that directly examines instructed emotion regulation (reappraise > look) and uninstructed viewing (look negative > look neutral) using visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look; look negative > look neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholding, and presents coordinate-based results. Sample is healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: instructed emotion regulation with reappraisal and selective attention; I7: visual stimuli — 40 s negative film clips; I8: acceptable sample including younger and older adults; I9: reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, here as PPI contrasts such as reappraisal > passive viewing and reappraisal > selective attention). However, it violates key requirements: the article reports only seed-based functional connectivity (PPI) analyses conducted within an a priori PFC/amygdala mask and does not present a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not met). Therefore exclusion criteria E5 (reports ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports only ROI/small-volume-masked results with no whole-brain analysis) apply. Note: the authors state that neural activity contrasts were reported previously (Allard & Kensinger, 2014), but those whole-brain activation results are not presented in this full text. Full text appears complete for this paper. Given E4 and E5, the study must be excluded.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using an explicit cognitive reappraisal instruction (ERT: Reappraise, Maintain, Look) with visual IAPS images. Full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment instructing emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) using visual IAPS pictures in healthy high-risk and control groups. This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs view) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) in adults with ADHD and matched healthy controls. Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI paper with whole-brain group-level results (meets I5, I8, I10, I11), it does NOT meet key topical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. The fMRI task is a placebo analgesia paradigm using thermal pain stimuli and expectancy manipulation, not an instructed emotion-regulation task with visual emotional stimuli. The independent cognitive reappraisal (CRA) lab task using visual images was performed outside the scanner and not used as an in-scanner regulation instruction; there is no within-fMRI contrast of an instructed regulation condition (e.g. reappraise > look) nor any visual-emotion stimulus regulation in the scanner. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7 and I9 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (instructed to reappraise vs view/maintain) using visual stimuli (negative and neutral pictures). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs an explicit emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and compares it with a placebo and passive viewing. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (static images) (I7). This paper reports a task-based fMRI study (Study 2) using an instructed cognitive reappraisal task (regulate vs experience vs observe) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) while presenting visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images).
